conventions.convention: Data points are rows; centering is left multiplication by H_n = I_n − 1_n 1_nᵀ/n, with n ≥ 1.
PCA minimizes centered Frobenius reconstruction error over p-by-q frames satisfying QᵀQ = I_q, with 1 ≤ q ≤ p; the reconstruction can have rank below q.
Nearest-neighbor lists exclude the subject index and sort by increasing (Euclidean distance, sample index). Union symmetrization uses either directed selection; mutual symmetrization requires both.
Kernel PCA assumes a symmetric positive-semidefinite input Gram matrix and returns eigenvectors scaled by square roots of centered eigenvalues, including zero coordinates when selected.
Classical MDS squares dissimilarities entrywise and retains at most q strictly positive eigenvalues; it returns fewer than q columns when necessary.
Local LLE weights may be signed, must sum to one, and are selected by minimum Euclidean norm among all affine reconstruction-error minimizers.
LLE returns no embedding unless ker(I−W) is exactly the constant subspace. Successful outputs satisfy Yᵀ1_n = 0 and YᵀY = I_q, with 1 ≤ q < n.
Metric stress sums squared distance residuals over unordered pairs i < j and is optimized over centered coordinates; it is distinct from classical MDS.

load_bearing.statement: For symmetric A with eigenvalues λ₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_p and 1 ≤ q ≤ p, tr(QᵀAQ) ≤ Σ_{j=1}^q λ_j whenever QᵀQ = I_q. Equality holds exactly for subspaces containing all eigenspaces above λ_q, orthogonal to those below λ_q, and using their remaining dimension in the λ_q eigenspace.
For n ≥ 1, H_n is symmetric and idempotent, annihilates 1_n, and is the orthogonal projection onto the zero-sum subspace.

For a fixed point and a nonempty finite neighbor list of distinct indices, affine least-squares reconstruction has a nonempty affine set of minimizers and exactly one minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer, including singular covariance cases, without a choice axiom.

For every symmetric nonnegative zero-diagonal D, B = −H_n D^{∘2} H_n/2 is symmetric and has a real orthonormal eigendecomposition. If D is Euclidean, B = Z_c Z_cᵀ, and coordinates from all positive eigenvalues recover every distance and are isometric to the centered configuration on their spans.
For n ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ k < n, select the first k other indices ordered lexicographically by (Euclidean distance, index), with the specified union, mutual, or radius graph construction.

For centered n-by-p data with n,p ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ q ≤ p, the minimum squared Frobenius reconstruction error over orthonormal q-frames is Σ_{j=q+1}^p σ_j², with precisely the stated top-eigenspace equality cases.

If W1_n = 1_n and ker(I−W) is the constant subspace, then for 1 ≤ q < n the minimum of tr(YᵀMY), subject to Yᵀ1_n = 0 and YᵀY = I_q, is the sum of the q smallest positive eigenvalues of M = (I−W)ᵀ(I−W), attained by corresponding orthonormal eigenvectors.
Finite Euclidean configurations with equal Gram matrices admit the well-defined onto linear isometry Σ c_i x_i ↦ Σ c_i y_i between their spans, including empty configurations.

published_dependencies.used_for: Euclidean positivity, bilinear Gram expansions, orthogonality, and squared-norm identities throughout the batch.
Identifying real symmetric matrices with self-adjoint endomorphisms before applying the spectral theorem.
Orthonormal eigendecompositions in Ky Fan maximization, centered kernel PCA, MDS, and LLE.
Diagonal-sum trace identities and the PCA/LLE objectives.
Rectangular trace cycling in the Ky Fan and PCA proofs.
The entrywise squared-error objective and its real trace expansion.
Right singular bases and the eigenvalues of X_cᵀX_c in PCA optimality.
The Frobenius squared norm equals the sum of squared singular values, used to evaluate the PCA error tail.
Existence and affine-kernel structure of local LLE reconstruction minimizers after parametrizing the affine constraint.
Selecting the unique least-norm member of an affine minimizer set and decomposing the LLE constant and zero-sum subspaces.
An orthonormal coordinate matrix for the zero-sum subspace in the LLE trace proof.
